preconditions.description: Attacker must have minter role (either be owner or be set as minter via setMinter function)
Attacker address must not be blacklisted

violation_target.exploit_hint: As a minter (owner or designated minter), call the mint() function with your address as the recipient and an arbitrary large amount (e.g., type(uint256).max). This will inflate the token supply and give you unlimited tokens that can be transferred or sold, devaluing the token for all other holders.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The CUSD contract has a mint() function protected by onlyMinter modifier. The minter can be either the owner or a designated minter address. The vulnerability allows unlimited token minting if the attacker gains minter privileges. Since we need to be either owner or minter, and setMinter() is onlyOwner, we need to become the owner first via storage manipulation.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite the owner slot in the CUSD contract to make address(this) the owner. 2. Call setMinter() to set ourselves as minter. 3. Call mint() with a large amount to mint unlimited tokens to our address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Find the owner storage slot in the contract (likely slot 0 based on inheritance order). 2. Use vm.store() to set owner to address(this). 3. Call setMinter(address(this)) to make ourselves the minter. 4. Call mint(attacker, largeAmount) to mint tokens. 5. Verify balance increased.
